name: Altstadt Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: Kufstein's historical old town charms visitors with the world-famous Römerhofgasse, Inn-Salzach architecture, and fortress views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historical Altstadt von Kufstein – Tyrol's second-largest city – is picturesquely nestled at the foot of the mighty fortress hill directly on the green waters of the Inn. As a border city between Tyrol and Bavaria, Kufstein looks back on an eventful history reflected in its winding alleys, traditional townhouses built in the Inn-Salzach style, and ancient defensive fortifications. Kufstein is internationally renowned as the setting for the world-famous Kufstein-Lied ("Die Perle Tirols"), whose traditional melodies are inextricably linked with legendary Römerhofgasse.

History & Architecture

Kufstein was granted town rights in 1393 by Duke Stephen III of Bavaria. For centuries, this strategically vital transportation hub on the edge of the Alps was fiercely contested between the Bavarian Wittelsbachs and the Tyrolean Habsburgs. In 1504, Emperor Maximilian I besieged the fortress and secured the town for Tyrol; today, the water bastion on the riverbanks of the Inn still recalls the late medieval city wall. The architectural jewel of the historic quarter is Römerhofgasse: with its elaborately decorated bay windows, artistic murals, wooden shingle roofs, and vaulted archways, this narrow lane presents a vivid picture of the 16th century. Here stands the historic tavern Auracher Löchl, where Karl Ganzer composed the Kufstein-Lied in 1947 – a monument in the alley pays tribute to the folk composer. Unterer Stadtplatz impresses with its colorful facades featuring horizontal parapet walls, the neo-Gothic town hall adorned with Tyrolean municipal crests, and the historic Marienbrunnen fountain.

Visit & Getting There

The pedestrian zone of Kufstein's old town is freely accessible around the clock all year without admission fees. Ascending to Festung Kufstein via the panoramic funicular or rock tunnel requires an admission ticket (day ticket for the fortress incl. Heldenorgel concert approx. €14.50 for adults). Daily at 12:00 noon (and at 18:00 in summer), the sound of the Heldenorgel – the largest outdoor organ in the world – resounds from the fortress across the alleys of the old town. By car: toll- and vignette-free from the north via the A93/A12 motorway to exits Kufstein Nord or Süd; central underground parking garages are located at Arkaden and Kultur Quartier. By public transport: Kufstein is a major international railway junction (ÖBB Railjet, ICE, Meridian). From Kufstein Hauptbahnhof, it takes only five minutes on foot across the Innbrücke bridge straight to Unterer Stadtplatz and into Römerhofgasse.

Tips

The pedestrian zones along Unterer and Oberer Stadtplatz and the riverside promenade along the Inn are level and barrier-free for wheelchair users and strollers; Römerhofgasse features somewhat uneven cobblestones but remains passable. Combine your stroll with a glass of fine wine at Auracher Löchl or visit the world's smallest bridge bar. The riverside walkway along the Inn offers fantastic photo opportunities of the historic old town skyline against the fortress cliff.
